verses.text: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “We're your own flesh and blood.
Even when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing it back. The LORD told you, ‘You'll shepherd my people Israel and become their ruler.’”
All Israel's elders came to King David at Hebron. He made a covenant with them there before the LORD, and they anointed him king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he became king. He reigned for forty years.
He ruled Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months. From Jerusalem he ruled all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.
The king and his men went to Jerusalem to fight the Jebusites who lived there. The Jebusites told him, “Even the blind and the lame will keep you out.” They thought David couldn't get into the city.
But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which became the City of David.

That day David said, “Whoever takes on the Jebusites must go up by the watercourse and strike those ‘lame and blind’ whom David hates.” That's where the saying comes from: “The blind and the lame can't enter the house.”
David moved into the stronghold and named it the City of David. He built up the area from the Millo inward.
David grew more and more powerful because the LORD, the God of Armies, was with him.
King Hiram of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar, carpenters, and stoneworkers. They built David a house.
David realized that the LORD had established him as Israel's king and had raised up his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
After moving from Hebron, David took more wives and concubines in Jerusalem. He had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all went looking for him. David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.
The Philistines had spread out across the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked the LORD, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” The LORD said, “Go up. I'll certainly hand them over to you.”
David went to Baal Perazim and defeated them there. He said, “The LORD broke through my enemies like water bursting through a barrier.” That's why he named the place Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their idols behind, and David and his men carried them away.
The Philistines came up again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked the LORD what to do. The LORD told him to go around behind the Philistines and come against them near the mulberry trees.
When he heard marching in the treetops, he was to move, because the LORD would have gone ahead of him to strike down the Philistine army.
David did what the LORD commanded and struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.
